about: The first part of the epilogue, which the stele carries after the last numbered law. It opens by saying what has gone before: these are the just decisions that Hammurabi, the capable king, established, by which he made the land hold to a firm way and good leadership (xl 1–8). The king then speaks of himself in the first person: the perfect king, to whom Ellil and Marduk gave the black-headed people to shepherd; he was not careless; with the weapon of Zamama and Ishtar, the wisdom of Ea and the power of Marduk he tore out the enemy above and below, put out the wars, and made the people lie down in safety (xl 9–41). He is the shepherd whose scepter is straight, whose good shade is spread over his city, who held Sumer and Akkad in his bosom; the strong may not wrong the weak, and the orphan and the widow are to be done right by (xl 42–69). To judge the cases of the land he wrote his weighty words on his stele and set it up before his statue, “King of Justice” (xl 70–78); he is pre-eminent among the city-kings, and by the command of Shamash he prays that justice may appear in the land and, by the word of Marduk, that no one efface his designs (xl 79–94). Column xli turns to the reader. A wronged man is to come before the statue, read the stele aloud, hear the words, see his case, and pray for the king, saying that Hammurabi was like a father to the people, revered Marduk’s word, won the victory, gladdened Marduk’s heart and set the land right; the guardian spirits and the gods of Esagila are to show favor before Marduk and Zarpanitum (xli 1–58). Then comes the charge to the king of the future: keep the words of justice written on my stele, and do not change the judgments and decisions I gave or efface my designs (xli 59–74; the charge continues in the next part). The numbers in the margin are the stele’s own line numbers, not law numbers. A few readings are uncertain; the notes say where (the ūsam/nūram of xl 21, aḫḫiša, īša, igirrê, danītam, the signs for “statue” and “brick”). Where the print alone does not show how Harper divides the lines (xl 65–69, xl 90–94, xli 25–33), the plate’s ruled lines confirm his division.

sentences.i: The just decisions that Hammurabi, the capable king, established,
sentences.n: The epilogue begins here, in a new column (xl). It opens like a heading: a noun phrase with no main verb of its own, “the judgments of justice” (dīnāt, the plural “judgments” in the form that stands before a genitive; mīšarim, “of justice”, genitive). The relative particle ša “which” then opens a clause about Hammurabi: ukīnūma is ukīn, the D-stem of kânum “to be firm” (D: “to make firm, to establish”), with the subjunctive -u that every verb in a ša-clause takes, and -ma “and”, which hooks this clause to the next unit. lēʾûm “capable, mighty” (Harper’s li-u-um; the litany spells the same word li-i-a-um). The king names himself in the third person here and moves to “I” at xl 9. Harper’s square brackets (as in later lines: wa-[aš]-tu-tim) mark signs he restores or is unsure of; I keep them in the signs.

Š-stem of ṣabātum “to seize, take hold”: to make seize, make take hold: ušaṣbitu (u-ša-az-bi-tu, preterite, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause) “he made (the land) take hold”; the Š verb takes two accusatives, the one made to seize and the thing seized; the z-sign stands for ṣ

sentences.i: and caused the land to take hold of a firm right way and good leadership.
sentences.n: The relative clause goes on: ušaṣbitu is the Š-stem (causative) of ṣabātum “to seize”, 3rd singular, again with the subjunctive -u: “he made (the land) seize”. A Š verb takes two accusatives, here three words in -am in a row: mātam “the land” is the one made to seize, and ūsam kīnam “a firm right way” and rīdam damqam “good leadership” are what it seizes. ūsum is Harper’s “help, assistance, support” (he lists this place, xl 21 and the prologue’s u-si-im under it); in the prologue and the litany we render it “right conduct” (compare the litany’s mātam ūsim šuḫuzim, “to give the land right conduct”), and I keep that here. rīdum is Harper’s ridu “government”, a noun of redûm “to lead”. damqam is Harper’s dam-ga-am (his damku “pure”): the usual word is damqum “good”, with q written by the GA sign. Uncertain: Harper’s u-sa-am has no caron visible on the page (our transcription of Harper’s print notes that it might be u-ša-am); the plate shows the SA sign, and ūsam is the word one expects in this phrase.

sentences.i: I am Hammurabi, the perfect king.
sentences.n: Here the king speaks in the first person, and that voice runs through the whole epilogue. This is a sentence with no verb: the name, the titles, and the pronoun anāku “I” held back to the end for emphasis (the Akkadian order is “Hammurabi, the perfect king — I”). gitmālum “perfect, complete” is the title the litany gave the king (mu-uš-ta-lum gi-it-ma-lum); Harper’s glossary has gitmalu “perfect”. This is the first of many lines of royal self-praise (“I am the shepherd who …”).

sentences.i: To the black-headed people whom Ellil gave me, and whose shepherding Marduk gave me,
sentences.n: This phrase is fronted: the king’s main verbs come in the next unit (“I was not careless”). SAG.GI₆ is a Sumerogram (a word written with Sumerian signs and read in Akkadian): it stands for ṣalmāt qaqqadim, “the black-headed people”, that is, mankind (our house rendering). Harper prints it SAG.GIG and reads it the same way; the plate sign after SAG is the MI sign, as in the prologue. {d}EN.LÍL is Ellil, the divine determinative {d} (the AN sign, read nothing) in front of the name; Harper calls him Bêl, “lord”, and his glossary gives “Bêl [EN.LIL]”. išrukam is išruk “he gave (as a gift)” (šarākum) plus the ventive -am “to me”, and iddinam is iddin “he gave” (nadānum) plus -am. ša marks the relative clause “whom (Ellil gave me)”. rēʾūssina is rēʾûtum “shepherdship, rule” (Harper: “government, guardianship”) plus -šina “their”, the ssi spelled with the ZI sign.

morph.gloss: not (in main clauses)

to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and” · igûma (i-gu-ma) “(who) was careless, and” (the preterite igi with the relative -u, as ilqû beside ilqe, then -ma) · īgīma (i-gi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he was careless, and”: malaḫum īgīma “the boatman was careless, and” · egû (e-gu, Harper’s reading of the 1st person) “I was careless”

not (in main clauses)

to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth” · addi (ad-di, preterite, 1st person) “I let drop”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop”, the idiom of aḫšu iddi

sentences.i: I was not careless, and I did not let my arm drop (I was never idle).
sentences.n: Two short denials of the king’s own conduct, each with ul “not” before the verb. egû is from egûm “to be careless, to neglect” (Harper’s e-gu, 1st person “I was careless”; compare itēgi in the laws). aḫī ul addi is “I did not let my arm drop”: aḫī is aḫum “arm” with -ī “my” (Harper files a-ḫi under aḫu “side”), and addi is “I threw, let fall” (nadûm). It is the idiom you met in the laws, aḫšu iddi “he let his arm drop”, which means he was idle (§44); here it is first person and negative: “I was never idle”.

sentences.i: I sought out places of peace for them; I opened up the difficult straits; I brought out help for them.
sentences.n: Three first-person clauses with no connecting “and” (the style of the self-praise). ešteʾišināšim: ešteʾi is the perfect “I have sought” of šeʾûm (the perfect, with the -t- after the first root letter; Harper’s I,2), plus the dative -šināšim “for them” (feminine plural, agreeing with ṣalmāt “the black-headed”, which is feminine plural). upetti is the D-stem of petûm “to open”, 1st person (Harper’s u-[pi]-it-ti); pušqī “straits, tight places” (Harper’s pusku) with waštūtim “difficult, steep” (Harper’s wastu). ušēṣi is the Š of waṣûm “to go out”: “I made go out, I brought out”; the Š and the pronoun are written together. Uncertain: ūsam. Harper prints [u]-si-am “help, support” (the same word as xl 6, where we say “right way”), but his own footnote 1 says “Better to read with Winckler, [nu-r]a-am”, i.e. nūram “light”; the litany has mušēṣi nūrim “who makes light rise”, a close parallel. On the plate the first sign is drawn in outline (damaged), so it is a restoration either way, and the next two signs are drawn whole; I keep Harper’s ūsam and give Winckler’s as the alternative (“I brought out light for them”).

sentences.i: with the mighty weapon that Zamama and Ishtar entrusted to me,
sentences.n: ina + noun is “with, by means of”, and what follows is another relative clause with ša. GIŠ.TUKUL is the Sumerogram for kakkum “weapon” (GIŠ “wood” plus a second sign; Harper prints only kakku and the glossary gives no spelling); the plate shows two signs there with no ending, the second a box with horizontal strokes like Harper’s List of Signs no. 187 (ku, tuk), which is our TUK; whether the scribe meant the sign TUKUL by it is not checked (TENTATIVE). The first is the wide GIŠ sign that also stands in GIŠ.PA-šu (xl 44). dannim is “mighty” (dannum, as in the prologue, “the strong”). Zamama is the war-god of Kish. Harper prints {ilu}ZA.MA(L).MA(L); I spell it as in the litany. {d}INANNA is Ištar: Harper reads the same sign Nanâ (“Ishtar of Uruk”), and I keep our usual Ištar. ušatlimūnim is the Š-stem of talāmum, which Harper glosses “to entrust” (a rare verb), with the ventive -nim “to me” and the plural -ū: “they (the two gods) entrusted to me”.

sentences.i: with the wisdom that Ea decreed for me, with the power that Marduk gave me,
sentences.n: The same “ina + noun + relative clause” pattern, twice. IGI.GÁL-im is igigallim, a Sumerogram (“wide of eye”) for “wisdom”; Harper normalizes it egigalim and glosses igigallu “intelligent, broad of vision”; the litany has the same word (mu-di IGI.GÁL-im “who knows wisdom”). {d}EN.KI is Ea, god of wisdom. išīmam is išīm “he decreed” (šâmum “to fix, decree”, the same verb that fixes destinies in the prologue; not the “buy” šâmum) plus the ventive -am “to me”. līʾūtim is “power, might” (Harper’s liʾūtu), the noun belonging to lēʾûm “capable” (xl 4). Our transcription of Harper’s print notes that the sixth letter of his egigalim is faint; the plate row has five signs, which fits i-na IGI.GÁL-im (confirmed).

sentences.n: A run of first-person verbs with nothing between them. assuḫ is “I tore out, uprooted” (nasāḫum), the verb the laws use of casting a son out of the family; it is written az-zu-uḫ, with the z-signs doing duty for s (Harper reads azzuḫ). elîš and šaplîš “above” and “below” (the ending -iš makes an adverb) together mean “everywhere”. qablātim “battles” is Harper’s gablu “battle”; the first sign GA is read qa₂, since the word is qablum. ubelli is the D-stem of balûm (Harper: I “to destroy”, II “to extinguish, to make an end of”): “I put out”. šīr mātim uṭīb is “the flesh of the land I made good”, the same phrase as the litany’s šīr nišī uṭīb (the prologue has ana šīr nišī ṭubbim); šīrum “flesh” here means bodily well-being, and ṭâbum D is “to make good”.

sentences.i: I am the shepherd, the protector, whose scepter is straight;
sentences.n: anākuma is anāku “I” with -ma, which here stresses the subject: “I indeed”. SIPA is the Sumerogram (PA plus LU) for rēʾûm “shepherd”, the picture of the king for his people. mušallimum is a D participle of šalāmum “to be whole”, so “one who keeps whole, safeguards” (Harper’s glossary: “guardian, protecting”). GIŠ.PA-šu is ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter” (GIŠ “wood” + PA, a staff; Harper prints ḫaṭṭu-šu); the stem sits in the Sumerogram, so the suffix -šu “his” is the only syllable written. The clause ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight” is a first example of the “whose … ” construction: ša, then a noun with its own possessive suffix, then the verb. išarat is from ešērum “to be straight, right”, 3rd person feminine (the scepter is “straight”, which also means “just”).

sentences.i: in Babylon, the city whose head Anum and Ellil raised high, in Esagila,
sentences.n: KÁ.DINGIR.RA{ki} is Bābilim “of Babylon” (“gate of the god”), with the place determinative {ki}; Harper prints KA.DINGIR.RA.KI. URU is ālum “city”, in apposition to Babylon; the relative clause ša … rēšīšu ullû “whose head they raised” is another “whose …” construction, with the verb last. ullû is the D of elûm “to go up”: “they raised high” (Harper’s “to raise on high”), 3rd plural; the two subjects are the high gods. AN is the bare AN sign (the plate shows the same star as the determinative), read Anum, the sky-god, as in the prologue and the litany: Harper prints ilim “a god” (his glossary files this line under ilu), but the pair with Ellil (Harper’s Bêl, here {d}EN.LÍL) points to Anum, and as one of the two subjects of ullû it is nominative. Esagila is Marduk’s great temple in Babylon. On the plate xl 65, 66 and 67 are separate ruled lines (ri-ši-šu / u-ul-lu-u / i-na Esagila), so Harper’s division stands.

sentences.n: Three purposes, each an infinitive (the first two after ana, the third, šūtešurim, standing without its own ana): dīānim “to judge” (dīānum), parāsim “to decide” (parāsum), šūtešurim “to set right”. sentences.n: lillikma is li + illik, the preterite of alākum “to go”, with -ma “and”: “let him go, and”. sentences.n: -mi is the particle of quoted speech: it hangs on the first word and says that what follows is spoken; the verb that introduces the speech is liqbīma, “let him say”, at xli 40. glossary.-šināti: them (3rd-person feminine plural accusative, on a verb): ušaršišināti “I let them get”, attabbalšināti “I carried them”, uštapṣiršināti “I sheltered them”; the dative is -šināšim
glossary.-šināšim: for them, to them (3rd-person feminine plural dative, on a verb): ešteʾišināšim “I sought for them”, ušēṣišināšim “I brought out for them”; the accusative is -šināti
glossary.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye” · after a t, on a verb: uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him” (the z of the stem + -šu said ss, spelled ZU); on nouns bīssu (É-ba/zu) “his house” and the participles murabbīšu, murabbītišu, murabbīssu “the one who raised him”; on a verb, ilqûšu, urtabbišu, urabbûšu, imtanûšu “him”; on the noun lišānšu (EME-šu) “his tongue”, īnšu “his eye”, mêšu “his waters”, mārūtišu “his sonship” · on a noun: bēlšu (be-el-šu), bēlišu (be-li-šu) “his master”, warḫušu (ITI-šu) “his month”, uznašu (u-zu-un-šu) “his ear”, nādinānšu (na-di-na-an-šu) “his seller”, nādinānišu (na-di-na-ni-šu) “his seller” after ana · written ZU in ARAD-zu, GEME₂-zu (warassu, amassu “his male slave, his female slave”) · on a verb, “him”: ukānšuma (u-ka-an-šu-ma) “he shall convict him, and” · also “its” on a Sumerogram or plural noun: GIŠ.PA-šu ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter”, SUḪUŠ-šu išdāšu “its foundations”, libbašu, libbišu “his heart”, bēlišu “his lord”, rēšīšu “its head”, dīnšu “his case”
glossary.Ea: Ea ({d}EN.KI) — god of wisdom and the deep
glossary.Enlil: Enlil ({d}EN.LÍL) — lord of the lands, chief of the pantheon’s executive
glossary.Esagila: Esagila, “House whose top is high” — Marduk’s temple in Babylon
glossary.Ištar: Ishtar — goddess of love and war; written {d}INANNA (Harper: Nanâ) or GIŠ.DAR (Harper: Anunit)
glossary.Zamama: Zamama ({d}ZA.MAL.MAL; modern Zababa) — warrior-god of Kish
glossary.Zarpanītum: Zarpanitum, the consort of Marduk (goddess, with the divine determinative {d}): {d}Zar-pa-ni-tum, the first syllable one sign (Harper’s List no. 183, zar), its sign key TENTATIVE
glossary.abum: father: ilik abišu “his father’s fief-duty” · abī (a-bi) construct “father of”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · abim written a-ba in bīt abim (Harper’s spelling, UNCERTAIN)
glossary.aburrum: safety, security (Harper’s aburru): aburrī (a-bu-ur-ri) “in safety”, taken as an adverb; the ending -ī is not explained by the grammar
glossary.almattum: widow (Harper almattu); written with the Sumerian signs NU.MU.SU and not spelled out, the ending is read from the context: almattum “a widow” (nominative, as subject of the law), almattim “of the widow” (genitive); in the sense “woman whose husband has died”
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and” · lillikma (li-il-li-ik-ma, li- + illik + -ma) “let him go, and”
glossary.amārum: to see, examine: immarūma “they shall examine” · ītamar “he has seen” (perfect, singular) · ītamar (i-ta-mar, perfect) “he saw”: lā ītamar “he did not see”; of a loss, “he met with”: bitiqtam ītamar “he met a loss”
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu) · also “over” (ana ālīya “over my city”), “before” in ana maḫar “into the presence of”; of time, ana dār “for ever”, ana warki “hereafter”, ana matīma “whenever”; ana lā + infinitive “so as not to”
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.ay: may not, let not (the negative-wish particle, Harper’s a “prohibitive”; written a, said ay), before a preterite: ay unakkir “may he not change”, ay ušazziq “may he not efface”, ay iršiā “may they not get”; it is not lā
glossary.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went”
glossary.aḫum: arm, side: aḫšu iddi “he let his arm drop” = he was idle, negligent · aḫī (a-ḫi) “my arm”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop” (aḫum + -ī “my”)
glossary.aḫum-brother: brother (aḫum): aḫḫū (aḫ-ḫu) “brothers” (nominative plural), aḫīšunu (a-ḫi-šu-nu) “their brother” (aḫum + -šunu “their”) · aḫḫūša (aḫ-ḫu-ša) “her brothers” (nominative plural + -ša), aḫḫīša (aḫ-ḫi-ša) “of her brothers” (genitive plural): ša aḫḫīšama “that of her brothers alone”, itti aḫḫīša “with her brothers”
glossary.balûm-D: D-stem of balûm (Harper: I “to destroy”, II “to extinguish”): to put out, make an end of (Harper: “to make an end of”): ubelli (u-bi-el-li, preterite, 1st person) “I put out”
glossary.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû · ibašši (i-ba-aš-ši, present) “there is, is upon”: ḫubullum elišu ibašši “a debt is upon him” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “has happened, has broken out”, of the plague in the pen: lipit ilim ittabši “a stroke of the god has happened” · ibaššû (i-ba-aš-šu-u, present with the subjunctive -u) “who is (to the people)”
glossary.bašûm-N: N-stem of bašûm: to be there, be found: ibbaššû (present, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “which are found” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “it has come about, has happened”
glossary.bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost · bēl (be-el) “owner of” before a genitive: bēl wardim “the owner of the male slave” · bēlī (be-li) “my master”: ul bēlī atta “you are not my master” · bēlšu, bēlišu (be-el-šu, be-li-šu) “his master”
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone · bīssu (É-ba(=zu): the plate sign is BA where ZU is meant) “his house”, the t of bītum and -šu said ss: bīssu ipuš “he has set up a house of his own”; bīt abišu “his father’s house” (É a-bi-šu), bīt written É alone
glossary.damāqum-D: D-stem of damāqum “to be good”: to show favor, be gracious (Harper’s damaku II “to favor”): lidammiqū (li-dam-mi-qu₂, precative, 3rd plural, KU read qu₂) “may they show favor”
glossary.dannum: the strong one: ina dīnim ana dannim ištarak “in a lawsuit he handed (him) to the strong”
glossary.danītum: UNCERTAIN: a solemn utterance (?) (Harper’s glossary: danitu “inscription, code”), or an adverb “firmly” from dannum “strong”; this part takes the adverb: danītam (da-ni-tam) “firmly (?)”
glossary.dīnum: case, lawsuit; judgment: dīn napištim “a case of life” · dīnāt (di-na-a-at, plural, the form before a genitive) “judgments of”; dīn mātim “the case of the land”
glossary.dīānum: judging, the giving of judgment (the infinitive of dânum “to judge”): dīānim (di-a-nim, genitive) “to judge”, after ana or without it
glossary.egirrûm: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s egirru “dreams, plans”, the sense in this line unclear: igirrê (i-gi-ir-ri-e, plural, oblique case)
glossary.egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and” · igûma (i-gu-ma) “(who) was careless, and” (the preterite igi with the relative -u, as ilqû beside ilqe, then -ma) · īgīma (i-gi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he was careless, and”: malaḫum īgīma “the boatman was careless, and” · egû (e-gu, Harper’s reading of the 1st person) “I was careless”
glossary.ekûtum: orphan, bereft (one) (Harper’s ekûtu), UNCERTAIN: ekûtam (NU.TUK, Sumerogram “the one who has not”, no ending written; the accusative -am is supplied)
glossary.elîš: above (adverb in -iš, from elûm “up”): elîš (e-li-iš); with šaplîš “below”, together “everywhere”
glossary.elûm-D: D-stem of elûm “to go up”: to raise high (Harper: “to raise on high”): ullû (u-ul-lu-u, preterite, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “they raised high”
glossary.erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2) · irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) “she enters” and īrubu (i-ru-bu) “she entered” — present and preterite with the subjunctive -u, after lāma “before” and ištu “after” · irrub (i-ir-ru-ub) “she shall enter” (present, 3rd feminine); irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) after inūma “when”; īrubma (i-ru-ub-ma) “she entered, and”, īrubu “(where) she entered”; erēbim (e-ri-bi-im) “of entering”, the infinitive in the genitive, in ana bītim šanîm erēbim “to enter another house”
glossary.ešērum: to be straight; Št-stem šutēšurum “to guide aright”; mušūšer · uštēšir (uš-te-še-ir, perfect) “he has set right”; šūtešurim (infinitive) “to set right”
glossary.galātum-D: D-stem of galātum (Harper’s galatu II “to molest”): mugallitam (mu-gal-li-tam, participle, accusative) “one who molests, terrifies”
glossary.gamrum: complete, whole (Harper: “complete, total”): gamrim (ga-am-ri-im), ana gamrim “for the whole”
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle” · also “with, by means of” (ina kakkim dannim “with the mighty weapon”, ina igigallim “with wisdom”), “by” with kibīt “command” and awāt “word” (the authority), “in” a manner (ina damiqtim “in favor”, ina šulmim “in peace”)
glossary.irnittum: victory (Harper’s irnittu): irnitti (ir-ni-ti, the form before a genitive) “victory of”
glossary.išdum: foundation (written with the single sign SUḪUŠ)
glossary.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay” · īša (i-na(=ša)) “he has”, UNCERTAIN: the carver wrote NA for ŠA and the form (īšu would be expected) is not accounted for
glossary.kakkum: weapon: kakkim (GIŠ.TUKUL, Sumerogram, no ending written; genitive after ina) “of the weapon”; Harper’s glossary gives no spelling, and the second sign (keyed TUK) is TENTATIVE
glossary.kalāmum-D: D-stem of kalāmum (Harper: KALAMU, “to show, inform”): to show: ukallam (u-kal-lam, present) “he shall show”
glossary.karābum: to bless, pray (for) (Harper): likrubam (li-ik-ru-ba-am, li- + ikrub + the ventive -am “for me”) “let him pray for me”
glossary.katātum-Š: Š-stem of a rare verb (Harper’s katatu III,2 “to give reverence to”), UNCERTAIN root: uštaktitma (uš-ta-ak-ti-it-ma, perfect, 3rd singular + -ma) “he has shown reverence, and”
glossary.kašādum: to reach, overcome: iktašassu “(the River) has overcome him”
glossary.kibītum: speech, command (Harper’s kibitu): kibīt (ki-be-it, the form before a genitive) “command of”
glossary.kânum: to be firm; D-stem kunnum — mukīn “who makes firm” · kīnā (ki-na, stative plural) “(they) are firm”; D preterite ukīn (u-ki-in) “I/he established, set up”, ukīnūma (with the subjunctive -u and -ma) “he established, and”
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · in place of, for (of animal for animal): alpam kīma alpim “an ox for an ox” (the §263 restitution)
glossary.kīnum: firm, true, steady (the adjective of kânum “to be firm”): kīnam (ki-nam, accusative) “firm”, said of ūsum “right conduct”
glossary.lamassum: the lamassu — protective guardian spirit (the KAL sign)
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her · ša libbiša (li-ib-bi-ša) “what is in her womb”, literally “that of her heart”, the unborn child: ana ša libbiša “for what was in her womb” · libbu (li-ib-bu) in ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land” (Harper’s form; after ina one would expect libbi)
glossary.libittum: brick, brickwork (Harper’s libittu): libit (SIG₄, Sumerogram, form before a genitive: libit Esagila “the brickwork of Esagila”); the sign is TENTATIVE
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see” · before an infinitive, ana lā ḫabālim “so as not to wrong”
glossary.līʾūtum: power, might (Harper’s liʾūtu), the noun of lēʾûm “capable”: līʾūtim (li-u-tim, genitive) “of power”, after ina “with power”; līʾūti (li-u-ti) the same noun in a hard clause where the case is UNCERTAIN
glossary.matīma: whenever, at any time (Harper’s matima “at the time, when”): ana matīma (ma-ti-ma); perhaps mati “when” + -ma, UNCERTAIN
glossary.maḫar: before, in the presence of: maḫar ilim “before the god”
glossary.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country”
glossary.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth” · addi (ad-di, preterite, 1st person) “I let drop”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop”, the idiom of aḫšu iddi
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause · inaddiššum (i-na-ad-di-iš-šum) “he shall give him” (inaddin + -šum, the n assimilated to š) · innadnušum (in-na-ad-nu-šum) “were given to him” (N-stem preterite + relative -u + -šum): ša innadnušum “that was given to him” · ittadin (it-ta-di-in) “he has given” (perfect): ana kaspim ittadin “he has sold for silver” · inaddin (i-na-ad-di-in-ma, inaddin + -ma) present “he shall give”: ana tamkārim inaddinma “he shall give to the merchant, and”
glossary.nakārum-D: D-stem of nakārum “to be strange, different”: to make different, change: uttakkir (ut-ta-ak-ki-ir, D perfect) “he has changed”: šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark (?)” (the object is UNCERTAIN; the verb is plain from the stem) · after ay: ay unakkir (u-na-ak-ki-ir, D preterite) “may he not change”
glossary.napāšum-D: D-stem of napāšum “to breathe, be at ease” (Harper’s napašu II “to set at ease”): linappišma (li-na-ab-bi-iš-ma, li- + nappiš + -ma (precative of the D); ab, bi read ap, pi₂) “let (his heart) be eased, and”; the shape and the subject (heart or man) are UNCERTAIN
glossary.narûm: stele, inscribed monument (Harper’s naru “monument, inscription”): narûya (na-ru-ia; also na-ru-i, with -ia “my” written short) “my stele”
glossary.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies
glossary.nazāqum-Š: Š-stem of nazāqum (Harper’s nazaku III “to cut off, efface, destroy”; the sense is not firm): to efface: mušazziqam (mu-ša-zi-qam, participle, accusative; KAM read qam) “one who effaces”, ušazziq (u-ša-zi-iq, preterite) “he effaced”; the stem and root are UNCERTAIN
glossary.našqum: weighty, choice (Harper’s našku): našqā (na-aš-qa₂, stative plural) “(they are) weighty” (GA read qa₂)
glossary.naṣārum: to guard, keep watch over, protect: inaṣṣarma (present, with -ma) “he shall guard, and …”
glossary.nemēqum: wisdom, skill (Harper’s nemequ): nemēqīya (ne-me-qi₂-ia) “my wisdom” (KI read qi₂)
glossary.parāsum: to decide, cut off: iprus · iparrasūma (i-par-ra-su-ma) “they shall investigate, and” (present plural + -ma; Harper: “to decide, to investigate, to inquire into”)
glossary.paṣārum-Š: Š-stem of paṣārum (Harper: “to hide, to restrain”; his III,2 form is the perfect): to shelter, protect (UNCERTAIN: “sheltered”, “protected” and “restrained” all fit): uštapṣiršināti (uš-tap-ṣi-ir-ši-na-ti, perfect, 1st person) “I have sheltered them”, with -šināti
glossary.petûm-D: D-stem of petûm “to open”: to open up, open wide: upetti (u-[pi₂]-it-ti, preterite, 1st person singular; the bracketed sign is Harper’s restoration) “I opened up”
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma · iqabbi (written i-qa₂-ab-bi-ma, iqabbi + -ma; Harper prints the GA sign as ga, read qa₂) present “he shall say, declare”: ina maḫar ilim … iqabbima “he shall declare before the god” · liqbīma (li-iq-bi-ma, li- + iqbi + -ma) “let him say, and”
glossary.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN
glossary.rabāṣum-Š: Š-stem of rabāṣum “to lie down, crouch”: to make lie down, make rest (Harper: “to make to rest”): ušarbiṣ (u-šar-be-iṣ, preterite, 1st person) “I made (them) lie down”
glossary.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired” · iršiā (ir-ši-a, 3rd feminine plural preterite) after ay “may (they) not get”, with uṣurātūa as subject
glossary.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN · ušaršišināti (u-šar-ši-ši-na-ti, 1st person) “I let them get”: mugallitam ul ušaršišināti “I let no molester have them”
glossary.râmum: to love: irammu (i-ra-am-mu, present), with the subjunctive -u after ša: ša irammu “whom he/she loves”
glossary.rēšum: head, top · rēš šattim (ri-eš ša-at-tim) “the start of the year”, literally “the head of the year”: ištu rēš šattim “from the start of the year”
glossary.rēʾûm: shepherd — here written with the Sumerogram SIPA · herdsman of cattle and sheep, the hired man of §264–267, written SIPA: rēʾûm “the herdsman” (rēʾûm, in the lost-herd laws); the signs are the same as for “shepherd”, and the Akkadian says herdsman as well
glossary.rēʾûtum: shepherdship, rule (Harper: “government, guardianship”), the abstract of rēʾûm “shepherd”: rēʾūssina (ri-u-zi-na) “their shepherding”, with the suffix -šina (t + š said ss, spelled with ZI)
glossary.rīdum: leading, guidance, government (Harper’s ridu “government”, a noun of redûm “to lead”): rīdam (ri-dam, accusative) “guidance”
glossary.tabālum: to take away, carry off: itabbal · tabal “take!” (imperative) · itbal (it-ba-al, preterite) “he took away” · itbalam (it-ba-lam, preterite + the ventive -am) “he has brought (it)”, the form that serves for “bring on”: ana abišu itbalam “he has brought (it) to his father”
glossary.talāmum-Š: Š-stem of talāmum “to entrust” (Harper’s glossary; a rare verb): ušatlimūnim (u-ša-at-li-mu-nim) “they entrusted to me” (preterite, plural -ū, with the ventive -nim “to me”)
glossary.tarāṣum: to stretch out, spread out (Harper’s glossary): tariṣ (ta-ri-iṣ, 3rd person singular) “it is spread out”; the form’s label (stative or other) is not settled
glossary.utlum: bosom, lap, side (Harper’s utlu): utlīya (ut-li-ia) “my bosom”
glossary.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u) · ūlissum (u-li-zum) “she bore him” (ūlid + -šum, d and š said ss; the last sign is one complex sign, its identification UNCERTAIN) · waldat (wa-al-da-at) “she has borne” (stative): ša mārī waldat “who has borne children”
glossary.wapûm-Št: Št-stem of wapûm “to appear”: to be made to appear, a passive sense (Harper lists it as III,2), UNCERTAIN: lištēpi (li-iš-te-bi, with li-, “let it be made to appear”; bi stands for pi₂); compare the Š-stem šūpûm “to make appear”
glossary.warki: after, behind: warkišu “after him, in his absence”
glossary.watārum-Š: Š-stem of watārum “to be in excess”: to surpass, be pre-eminent (Harper’s šuturu “pre-eminent”): šūturu (šu-tu-ru) “(is) pre-eminent”, a stative
glossary.waštum: difficult, steep (Harper’s wastu): waštūtim (wa-[aš]-tu-tim, feminine plural, oblique case; the bracketed sign is Harper’s restoration) “difficult”, said of pušqum “straits”; the sense rests on Harper’s glossary alone
glossary.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city”
glossary.zakārum-N: N-stem of zakārum “to name, mention” (Harper IV,1): passive: lizzakir (li-iz-za-ki-ir, li- + izzakir) “may it be named, be spoken of”
glossary.ālum: city (URU): ālum u rabiānum “the city and the mayor”
glossary.Šamaš: Shamash ({d}UTU) — the sun-god, lord of justice
glossary.ša: who, which, of · also “whose”: ša + a noun with its own suffix + the verb at the end (ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight”), the verb in the subjunctive
glossary.šalāmum-D: D-stem of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make good, restore (Harper: “to restore”): ušallamma (u-ša-lam-ma) “he shall make good, and”
glossary.šanānum: to rival (Harper’s šananu): šāninam (ša-ni-nam, accusative) “a rival”; the clause it stands in is UNCERTAIN
glossary.šaplîš: below (adverb in -iš, from šaplum “lower part”): šaplîš (ša-ap-li-iš); with elîš “above”
glossary.šar ālim: “king of the city” — Harper’s reading of the recurring pair LUGAL.URU-lim
glossary.šarrum: king: šarrum “the king”, šar-ri-im “of the king”
glossary.šarākum: to give away, hand over: ištarak · išruk (iš-ru-uq) “he has given (as a gift)” (the last sign UG, read uq or uk)
glossary.šasûm-Gt: Gt-stem of šasûm “to call, cry out” (Harper: “to speak, tell, read”): to read aloud: lištassīma (li-iš-ta-aš-si-ma, li- + ištassi + -ma) “let him read aloud, and”
glossary.šaṭrum: written, inscribed (the passive participle of šaṭārum “to write”): šaṭram (ša-aṭ-ra-am, accusative) “inscribed”, said of narûm “stele”
glossary.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document” · išṭurušim (iš-tu-ru-ši-im, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause), išṭuršim (iš-tur-ši-im), išṭuršimma (iš-tur-ši-im-ma) “he wrote for her (and)”, preterite + -šim: ina ṭuppim ša išṭurušim “in the tablet which he wrote for her”, lā išṭuršimma “he has not written for her, and”
glossary.šemûm: to hear, obey; šēmû “obedient (to)”; Š-stem muštešmi “who makes obey”
glossary.šeʾûm: to seek (Harper): ešteʾišināšim (eš-te-i-ši-na-šim) “I have sought for them”, the G perfect (the -t- infix; 1st person singular) + the dative -šināšim; not šeʾum “grain”
glossary.šulmum: peace, well-being, safety: šulmim (šu-ul-mi-im, genitive) “of peace”, and “in peace” after ina
glossary.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys” · ALSO a second verb of the same spelling, “to fix, decree” (destinies, well-being): išīm (i-ši-im) “he decreed”, išīmam (i-ši-ma-am) “he decreed for me” (preterite + the ventive -am)
glossary.šēdum: protective spirit, genius (Harper’s sedu “divinity”); the pair of lamassum: šēdum (še-du-um, nominative)
glossary.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
glossary.šūqurum: precious, weighty (Harper reads šukuru); UNCERTAIN: šūqurātim (šu-qu₂-ra-tim, feminine plural, oblique case) “weighty”, said of awātum “words”, KU read qu₂
glossary.ūmišam: daily, each day (adverb in -išam, from ūmum “day”): ūmišam (UD-mi-ša-am)
glossary.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277
glossary.Ḫammurabi: Hammurabi, king of Babylon c. 1792–1750 BCE (Amorite name, “the kinsman is great”)
glossary.ḫabālum: to wrong, oppress: iḫtabal “he has oppressed (a soldier)” — the very verb of the prologue’s promise
glossary.ṣabātum-Š: Š-stem of ṣabātum “to seize, take hold”: to make seize, make take hold: ušaṣbitu (u-ša-az-bi-tu, preterite, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause) “he made (the land) take hold”; the Š verb takes two accusatives, the one made to seize and the thing seized; the z-sign stands for ṣ
glossary.ṣalmum: statue, image (Harper’s salmu): ṣalmīya (ALAN-ia) “my statue”; the sign ALAN is TENTATIVE, the word being unspelled in Harper’s glossary
glossary.ṣillum: shade, shelter, protection (Harper’s silu “protection”): ṣillī (ṣi-li) “my shade” (the -ī is “my”)
glossary.ṣātum: future time, eternity (Harper’s satu): ṣāt (a(=ṣa)-at, the form before a genitive; the carver wrote A for ṢA, which Harper corrects): ṣāt ūmī “the future of days”
glossary.ṭâbum: to be good, pleasing; D-stem ṭubbum “make good”; muṭīb “gladdener” · ṭābu (ṭa-bu, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) is pleasing”: eliša ṭābu “it is pleasing to her” · ṭābum, ṭābam (ṭa-bu-um, ṭa-ba-am) “good”, adjective, nominative and accusative; uṭīb (u-ṭi-ib, D preterite) “I/he made good”
